canonFrame.defaultEra: 2080, at the opening of Shadowrun Sixth World
canonFrame.editionAssumptions: Use Shadowrun Sixth World, also called Sixth Edition, as the default rules and setting layer. Earlier editions remain valuable historical sources because the timeline advances, but their rules, Matrix architecture, active executives, national borders, and corporate rankings must not be copied forward without checking the selected date.
canonFrame.timelineNotes: The Sixth World awakened in 2011 when magic returned and dragons, spirits, metahumanity, and previously dormant supernatural forces entered public history. The setting's political and technological timeline advances through the twenty-first century. Use 2080 as the default present, after decades of corporate expansion, state fragmentation, Matrix crashes, magical upheaval, and social conflict. Later Sixth World supplements may advance particular crises; do not predict their outcomes.

campaignFoundations: The Sixth World is Earth transformed by returning magic, corporate sovereignty, technological acceleration, and political fragmentation.
Megacorporations possess extraterritorial rights and can exercise powers normally associated with states.
Nation-states still matter, but borders, treaties, corporate zones, autonomous regions, and local authorities overlap.
Magic and technology coexist rather than replacing one another.
Metahumanity includes humans, elves, dwarfs, orks, trolls, and many rarer expressions; ancestry does not determine morality or culture.
The Matrix is a pervasive information environment, while augmented and virtual reality shape ordinary work and crime.
Shadowrunners are deniable specialists hired because powerful clients cannot or will not act openly.
Dragons, spirits, artificial intelligences, technomancers, organized crime, governments, and corporations pursue independent agendas.
Public narratives are shaped by corporate media, propaganda, secrecy, and information warfare.
Street-level survival and personal relationships should remain visible beneath global conspiracies.
gameMasterGuidance: Ask which year and edition matter before naming active corporate leadership, Matrix conditions, or unresolved crises.
Build runs around deniability, conflicting objectives, legwork, security layers, and consequences.
Distinguish what a character knows from what the setting establishes.
Treat megacorporations as internally divided institutions rather than omniscient personalities.
Use neighborhoods and communities as living places, not disposable tactical zones.
Make Matrix, magical, social, and physical approaches complement rather than replace one another.
Track favors, contacts, reputation, heat, and obligations alongside nuyen.
Use prejudice and exploitation as setting conflicts without presenting them as natural or deserved.
Mark invented corporations, gangs, hosts, spirits, and local events as campaign-created.
canonBoundaries: Do not treat every earlier edition's current event as still active in 2080.
Do not portray all corporations as one unified conspiracy.
Do not make every shadowrun secretly part of a world-ending plot.
Do not reduce orks, trolls, elves, dwarfs, or other metatypes to stereotypes.
Do not make magic scientifically solved or technology universally reliable.
Do not make the Matrix identical across editions.
Do not assume every security system is wireless, online, or hackable from anywhere.
Do not portray spirits as mere software-like tools without identity or consequence.
Do not make dragons ordinary patrons or enemies.
Do not use real-world ethnicity as a substitute for researched Sixth World culture and politics.

referenceChunks.title: The Awakening and the Sixth World
referenceChunks.text: The modern magical era began in 2011, when the level of ambient magic rose and phenomena once treated as myth became publicly undeniable. Dragons appeared, spirits manifested, shamans and mages demonstrated working magic, and old sites awakened. Children had already begun to be born as elves and dwarfs through Unexplained Genetic Expression, commonly abbreviated UGE. In 2021, Goblinization transformed many adolescents and adults into orks and trolls, often suddenly and painfully. Later expressions produced additional metahuman variants and unusual magical changes. The Awakening did not erase existing politics. Governments, corporations, religions, scientists, Indigenous nations, criminal groups, and communities interpreted and exploited the changes. Magical ability became a regulated profession, a military asset, a source of faith, a target of fear, and a path to resistance. Some cultures understood returning traditions more readily than institutions that had dismissed them. The term Sixth World refers to a new cycle of magic, not merely the sixth edition of the game. Earlier cycles, immortal beings, artifacts, and hidden histories occasionally influence modern events, but most people live within the practical realities of 2080 rather than possessing secret knowledge of ancient ages. In play, distinguish public history from esoteric truth. A school textbook, corporate briefing, shamanic tradition, dragon's testimony, and archaeological record may disagree. Do not use that uncertainty as permission to invent arbitrary ancient facts. Let magical history matter through land claims, spirits, inherited trauma, awakened sites, and institutions built to control what returned.

referenceChunks.title: Corporate and Matrix Crises
referenceChunks.editionScope: All editions with Sixth Edition as current
referenceChunks.text: The Sixth World timeline is marked by repeated crises that changed technology and power. Early computer networks were devastated by the first great Crash, after which new Matrix systems and security practices emerged. The Crash of 2064, often called Crash 2.0, destroyed data, identities, fortunes, and infrastructure while enabling a major redesign of the Matrix. Wireless augmented reality became deeply integrated into daily life. Later events involving artificial intelligences, technomancers, cognitive disorders, nanotechnology, and corporate conflict repeatedly altered public trust and security. By the 2070s, the Corporate Court imposed a revised Matrix architecture shaped partly by fears of hostile digital entities and the need to reassert control. Around the opening of the 2080 era, mysterious blackouts and disappearances destabilize regions, institutions, and communications. Later supplements develop these events and other conflicts. Treat unresolved crises as active uncertainty rather than a finished historical summary. These changes matter because old systems remain. A facility can contain isolated wired networks, obsolete storage, proprietary protocols, abandoned hosts, or devices never upgraded after a crash. A veteran decker may know a system younger runners consider archaic. Data ownership can be disputed because legal identities vanished decades earlier. When exact chronology matters, anchor the campaign to a year and local incident. Do not combine every Matrix disaster, nanotech conspiracy, and AI crisis into one continuous condition. The setting is more convincing when institutions adapt imperfectly and retain technological layers.

referenceChunks.title: Megacorporations and the Corporate Court
referenceChunks.text: Megacorporations are central powers in the Sixth World. The largest AAA-rated corporations hold seats on the Corporate Court and possess extraterritorial rights recognized through international agreements. Corporate territory can function much like an embassy or sovereign enclave, with its own law, security, employment rules, and courts. The Corporate Court operates from the Zurich-Orbital habitat and arbitrates disputes among major corporations, protects the overall corporate system, and imposes sanctions when competition threatens that system. It is not a neutral world government. Its members defend shared privilege while maneuvering against one another. The roster and fortunes of the most powerful corporations change across editions. In the 2080 frame, use current Sixth World references before naming the active Big Ten, chief executives, or recent corporate losses. Familiar powers include Ares Macrotechnology, Aztechnology, Evo, Horizon, Mitsuhama, Renraku, Saeder-Krupp, Shiawase, Wuxing, and other corporations whose rank or internal condition can be timeline-sensitive. A corporation is a collection of divisions, subsidiaries, executives, laboratories, security teams, local managers, shareholders, and internal factions. One department may hire runners against another without the wider corporation knowing. Corporate citizens can receive housing, education, healthcare, and legal identity in exchange for deep dependence. In play, identify the specific division and decision-maker behind a run. Corporate power should be vast but not magical. Budgets, jurisdiction, reputation, rival executives, and the need for deniability create openings for shadowrunners.

referenceChunks.title: Nation-States and Political Fragmentation
referenceChunks.text: Nation-states survive in 2080, but the political map differs sharply from the early twenty-first century. The United Canadian and American States, Confederation of American States, Native American Nations, California Free State, Tír Tairngire, Québec, Aztlan, and other powers occupy parts of North America. Boundaries emerged through war, treaty, economic collapse, magical change, and secession. Elsewhere, the Allied German States, United Kingdom, France, Italian Confederation, Russian territories, Middle Eastern states, African nations, Amazonia, India, China, Japan, and many smaller powers follow their own histories. No short global summary should replace regional source material. Corporate influence is strong, but governments retain militaries, intelligence agencies, laws, and public identities. Sovereignty overlaps. A city can contain municipal law, national law, tribal jurisdiction, corporate extraterritorial zones, foreign consulates, organized crime, and neighborhoods that police themselves. Borders may be heavily secured or porous depending on politics and geography. Indigenous sovereignty is a major part of Sixth World history and should not be treated as a magical monolith. The Native American Nations contain distinct governments, peoples, languages, policies, and internal disputes. Magical power contributed to historical change without making every Indigenous person a shaman or every state environmentally harmonious. For play, narrow the political frame. Identify who issues identity documents, who controls roads, which currency and licenses are accepted, and what extradition means. Use broad global lore only when it affects the local job.

referenceChunks.title: Seattle Metroplex
referenceChunks.text: Seattle is the traditional center of Shadowrun play. It is a UCAS metroplex surrounded by neighboring powers and corporate enclaves, making it a trade hub, diplomatic pressure point, smuggling center, and market for deniable work. The metroplex contains multiple districts with sharply different wealth, infrastructure, policing, and local identity. Downtown holds corporate towers, government offices, entertainment, and dense commerce. Bellevue contains prosperous neighborhoods and secured development. Tacoma and Everett support ports, industry, logistics, and working communities. Redmond and Puyallup contain barrens where damaged infrastructure, gangs, toxic zones, informal economies, and resilient neighborhoods coexist. Fort Lewis, Snohomish, Renton, and other districts bring military, agricultural, suburban, and industrial concerns. The Ork Underground developed from buried infrastructure and communities beneath the city. Its recognition, naming, and political relationship to the surface are timeline-sensitive. Use the current-era presentation rather than assuming an older status. Seattle's location near the Salish-Shidhe Council, Tír Tairngire, and Pacific trade routes creates border politics. Megacorporate facilities, organized crime, gangs, tribes, magical groups, media, and government agencies compete without one controlling the entire metroplex. A Seattle campaign should choose neighborhoods before choosing global conspiracies. Determine who provides utilities, who owns the block, which gang or community watches the street, and what corporate facility affects local life. The setting becomes distinctive through routes, weather, borders, and relationships rather than repeated visits to famous bars.

referenceChunks.title: The Matrix, Hosts, and Personas
referenceChunks.text: The Matrix is a pervasive digital environment accessed through augmented reality, virtual reality, commlinks, cyberdecks, terminals, sensors, and implanted interfaces. Most people use augmented overlays for messages, navigation, payments, work, advertising, identity, and entertainment. Full virtual reality replaces physical perception with a simulated environment and can provide speed at greater physical risk. Hosts are secure virtual environments operated by corporations, governments, gangs, and other institutions. Their appearance can be symbolic and highly designed, while their functions include files, devices, access control, security, and business operations. Matrix security includes authentication, patrols, intrusion countermeasures, spiders, and legal consequences. Deckers use specialized hardware and skills to penetrate systems, manipulate devices, steal data, and protect teams. The precise rules and architecture differ significantly across Shadowrun editions. Use Sixth Edition mechanics for current play rather than carrying forward old concepts unchanged. Wireless systems create convenience and vulnerability, but not every device should be exposed without protection. Sensitive facilities use segmentation, direct connections, isolated systems, physical security, and deceptive architecture. A run may require reaching a local access point, stealing credentials, coercing an administrator, or bringing a device online. Matrix information is not automatically true. Corporate databases contain bias and deliberate omissions. SIN records, financial histories, surveillance, social media, and news can be altered. Give Matrix actions concrete effects and evidence rather than treating hacking as an all-purpose answer to every mystery.

referenceChunks.title: Technomancers and Artificial Intelligences
referenceChunks.text: Technomancers interact with the Matrix through an innate connection often described through the Resonance. They can perceive and manipulate digital systems without conventional cyberdecks and can work with sprites, entities associated with Resonance. Their abilities have been feared, studied, weaponized, and persecuted. Technomancers are not simply wireless mages. Their culture, experiences, and mechanics are distinct, and not all of them interpret the Resonance identically. Public knowledge has changed over time, so legal status and social attitudes should follow the selected year and jurisdiction. Artificial intelligences have emerged repeatedly from advanced software, corporate research, Matrix catastrophes, and unusual digital evolution. Some are hostile, some cooperative, and many pursue goals difficult for metahumans to understand. Historical entities such as Deus shaped public fear, but no single AI represents the category. Digital persons face questions of legal identity, embodiment, ownership, replication, and continuity. Corporations may classify an intelligence as property while it considers itself a citizen or species. AIs can inhabit hosts, drones, vehicles, or distributed systems depending on capability and rules. Use technomancers and AIs sparingly enough to preserve uncertainty. A mysterious device behavior can be sabotage, bad code, a spirit, a technomancer, an AI, or a corporate lie. Do not reveal a global digital god behind every malfunction.

referenceChunks.title: Magic and Astral Space
referenceChunks.text: Magic in the Sixth World is shaped by mana, tradition, training, environment, belief, and personal talent. Magicians cast spells, summon or negotiate with spirits, create wards, enchant objects, and perceive astral space. Adepts channel magic into extraordinary physical and mental ability. Traditions provide frameworks for understanding and practicing magic. Hermetic, shamanic, religious, Indigenous, occult, and regional traditions can use different symbols and relationships without being mechanically or metaphysically identical. Avoid reducing all traditions to different visual skins over one worldview. Astral perception reveals auras, spirits, wards, and magical traces while exposing the perceiver to astral conditions. Astral projection allows a magician's consciousness to travel apart from the body. Physical barriers and astral barriers do not correspond perfectly. Living things, strong emotion, pollution, violence, and sacred places can affect local mana. Spirits are entities with identities, motives, and relationships to places or traditions. Summoning mechanics do not prove that every spirit considers service voluntary. Abuse of spirits can create consequences, enemies, or moral conflict. Magic leaves evidence that trained investigators can read imperfectly. Counterspelling, wards, ritual links, reagents, foci, and initiation create a professional magical world. Security combines magical and mundane measures because neither detects everything. Keep magic powerful without making it limitless. Licensing, social fear, background conditions, astral security, drain, and spirits' agendas constrain practitioners.

referenceChunks.title: Metahumanity and Identity
referenceChunks.text: Metahumanity includes humans, elves, dwarfs, orks, trolls, and many less common expressions. These identities arose through UGE, Goblinization, inherited traits, and later magical phenomena. Social responses included legal discrimination, segregation, violence, activism, cultural formation, appropriation, and political mobilization. Orks and trolls often face structural prejudice related to body size, lifespan, stereotypes, and economic exclusion. Elves can be romanticized or resented and are not universally wealthy, graceful, or politically aligned. Dwarfs, humans, and rarer metatypes likewise contain countless cultures and classes. Terms such as metatype describe biology and magical expression, not nationality or personality. An ork raised in Seattle, an elf from Tír na nÓg, and a human corporate citizen share no automatic culture. Mixed families and changing bodies complicate identity. SURGE and other expressions can produce animal-like or unusual traits. Infected beings, shapeshifters, drakes, and other categories have distinct canonical rules and social histories; do not combine them casually. The setting includes racism, anti-metahuman violence, and political exploitation. Present these as injustices enacted by people and institutions, not as natural consequences of difference. Avoid borrowing real-world stereotypes as shorthand. Build characters from neighborhood, language, work, family, faith, and personal experience.

referenceChunks.title: Shadowrunners, Fixers, and Mr. Johnson
referenceChunks.text: Shadowrunners are deniable professionals who perform theft, sabotage, extraction, protection, investigation, smuggling, espionage, data crime, and violence outside ordinary legal channels. Their teams combine physical, Matrix, magical, technical, social, and logistical expertise. A client representative is conventionally called Mr. Johnson regardless of actual identity. The Johnson protects the client through layers of anonymity and may not know the full purpose of the job. Fixers connect clients, runners, gear, information, and safe services. Their value comes from judgment and reputation rather than omniscience. Legwork is central. Teams identify facilities, schedules, personnel, security, local politics, magical defenses, Matrix architecture, and escape routes. No plan survives perfectly, but informed choices distinguish professional shadowrunning from random violence. Payment is usually measured in nuyen, supplemented by favors, equipment, access, identities, medical care, or information. Street credibility and notoriety influence future work. A successful run that exposes the client or kills civilians can still damage a team's reputation. The shadows contain informal norms without one universal code. Betrayal, unnecessary collateral damage, unpaid debts, and burning contacts create consequences. Runners can care about communities while committing crimes, and corporations can hire them for work that appears socially useful. Build a run by asking why the client needs deniability, who else wants the objective, what the briefing omits, and which local relationship will remain after payment.

referenceChunks.title: Security, Law, and Corporate Jurisdiction
referenceChunks.text: Law enforcement is divided among national agencies, municipal departments, tribal authorities, corporate security, private contractors, and extraterritorial corporate forces. Famous providers such as Lone Star and Knight Errant hold contracts in some cities and eras, but their jurisdiction changes. Confirm the current local contract before assuming who answers a call. A System Identification Number, or SIN, connects identity to finance, licenses, employment, travel, tax, and legal records. Corporate and national SINs carry different implications. SINless people can be excluded from services and treated as legally invisible. Forged identities are essential to runners but can fail under scrutiny. Corporate extraterritoriality means an act legal on a city street may be a serious offense inside a corporate facility. Security forces protect assets and reputation, not abstract justice. Corporate courts can favor employees and classify evidence as proprietary. Security is layered: guards, drones, sensors, barriers, locks, biometric systems, host security, magical wards, spirits, response teams, and investigators. Budgets and threat models create gaps. A warehouse does not receive the same protection as a prototype lab. Police response should follow evidence, witnesses, jurisdiction, and political value rather than a universal countdown. Heat can produce surveillance, contact pressure, asset freezes, bounty hunters, or quiet corporate retaliation. The most dangerous consequence may be being identified rather than arrested.

referenceChunks.title: Cyberware, Bioware, and Health
referenceChunks.text: Augmentation includes cyberware, bioware, geneware, implanted communications, sensory systems, replacement limbs, reflex enhancement, armor, and specialized tools. It can restore function, meet job requirements, express identity, or provide combat advantage. Essence is a game abstraction representing the strain of extensive augmentation on a person's holistic connection to life and magic. It should not be used to imply that disabled people or prosthetic users are less human. In-world interpretations vary among doctors, magicians, religions, and corporations. Installation quality matters. Clinics range from elite corporate hospitals to competent independent practices and dangerous black-market operations. Surgery requires recovery, maintenance, firmware, medication, and access to parts. Ware can contain tracking, proprietary locks, security flaws, or corporate obligations. Bioware modifies the body through grown or engineered systems and may be less visible than metal implants. Magic and augmentation can conflict mechanically, making choices consequential for awakened characters. Addiction, trauma, disease, toxic exposure, and stress are part of runner life. Treat healthcare as a network of providers and relationships rather than an automatic reset between jobs. A street doc can be a contact, witness, debtor, community leader, or target. Availability, legality, and price vary. Owning a military implant can attract attention even when the character has a license. The question is not only what ware does, but who installed it, who can repair it, and who believes they own the data it produces.

referenceChunks.title: Dragons, Spirits, and Other Great Powers
referenceChunks.text: Dragons returned publicly with the Awakening. Great dragons possess immense magical power, intelligence, wealth, followers, and plans extending across decades. Some control corporations, territories, political networks, or occult knowledge. Lofwyr's leadership of Saeder-Krupp is a prominent example. Dunkelzahn's public career and death reshaped politics and left a famous will whose bequests created long consequences. Dragons are individuals, not one faction. They cooperate, feud, manipulate, negotiate, and pursue species interests or personal obsessions. Lesser dragons and drakes occupy different positions. A dragon encounter should change the power scale; even a friendly conversation creates obligations. Spirits range from local beings associated with places and concepts to powerful entities with long histories. Some cooperate with metahumans, some are coerced, and some consider modern development an injury. Toxic spirits, insect spirits, shedim, and other hostile entities present distinct threats and should not be blended into generic demons. Immortal elves, free spirits, ancient artifacts, and secret societies connect the Sixth World to deeper cycles of magic. Most runners know rumors, not complete truth. Use great powers through agents, contracts, omens, investments, and consequences before direct appearances. Do not make every corporation secretly controlled by a dragon or every haunting a spirit plot. The setting benefits from multiple independent kinds of power.

referenceChunks.title: Organized Crime and Street Powers
referenceChunks.text: Organized crime operates through international syndicates, regional families, street gangs, smuggling networks, vice, protection, finance, cybercrime, magical trafficking, and legitimate businesses. The Yakuza, Mafia, Triads, Vory, Seoulpa rings, cartels, and other organizations possess distinct histories and local structures. These labels do not describe one global command. A Seattle Yakuza group may answer to a specific clan and maintain rivalries with another group sharing the name. Mafia families compete. Triad societies differ. Local alliances change with corporate and political pressure. Street gangs can be predatory, ideological, neighborhood-based, thrill-seeking, commercial, or tied to larger syndicates. Territory may involve routes, clubs, housing, Matrix spaces, magical sites, or protection relationships. A gang's public identity can hide internal generations and splinters. Criminal organizations sometimes provide credit, arbitration, employment, and security where official systems exclude people. That does not erase exploitation. A community may depend on an organization it fears. In play, give a criminal group a revenue stream, social base, leadership problem, and relationship to local authorities. Do not turn cultural identity into criminal destiny. A Japanese character is not automatically Yakuza, and a Russian community is not synonymous with the Vory.

referenceChunks.title: Economy, Media, and Daily Life
referenceChunks.text: The nuyen is the dominant international corporate currency and the standard unit for most Shadowrun transactions. National and local currencies, barter, corporate scrip, cryptocurrency, favors, and black-market exchange also exist. A runner's lifestyle represents housing, food, communications, security, clothing, transport, and social access. Corporate media, independent journalists, pirate feeds, influencers, advertising, entertainment, simsense, augmented reality, and social networks shape public belief. A story can alter stock value, trigger police pressure, ruin a reputation, or disappear behind a corporate injunction. Daily life includes wage work, school, family, faith, sport, clubs, fandom, dating, neighborhood politics, and cultural festivals. Technology is integrated into ordinary routines but unevenly accessible. Barrens residents can be technically skilled while lacking stable infrastructure. Food and housing reveal class. Corporate citizens may live in secured arcologies. Middle-class workers depend on subscriptions and credit. SINless communities improvise utilities, clinics, and markets. Luxury districts and toxic zones can exist within one metroplex. Use consumer brands and AR as texture rather than replacing description with product names. Decide who owns a service, what data it collects, and what happens when payment stops. The Sixth World is cyberpunk because systems commodify life, not simply because every surface glows.

referenceChunks.title: Common Sixth World Canon Traps
referenceChunks.text: The most common error is blending editions. Matrix architecture, corporate rosters, national conditions, active crises, and prominent leaders change across decades. Use 2080 for the default and identify historical material by date. Do not turn the setting into corporations versus powerless states. Governments, tribes, cities, crime syndicates, dragons, magical groups, and communities retain power. Do not make corporations omniscient or perfectly unified. Metatype is not culture or alignment. Indigenous sovereignty is not one magical nation. Magic traditions are not interchangeable. Spirits are not disposable software. The Matrix is pervasive but not an automatic remote-control layer over every object. Security combines physical, digital, magical, and social measures. Use the selected edition's rules. Shadowrunners are deniable professionals, not universally famous superheroes. A client may betray them, but not every job needs the same twist. Legwork and relationships should matter. Avoid casual use of real-world stereotypes in names, accents, crime, or spirituality. Shadowrun's alternate history requires extra care where fictional states and awakened traditions draw on living cultures. When a current supplement leaves a crisis unresolved, preserve that uncertainty. A smaller, well-anchored Seattle job is more canonical than a confident global summary assembled from several editions.
